name: Rhesa
overview: Rhesa is a male figure mentioned in the lineage of the Messiah, as recorded in Luke 3:27. While his tribal affiliation and additional notes are not specified, his inclusion in this genealogy highlights his role in the ancestral line leading to Jesus Christ. This connection underscores his importance within the biblical narrative of redemption.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Rhesa' appears as a proper name in Luke 3:27. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided in the Scripture, so it is presented plainly without additional interpretive significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Rhesa was the son of Joanan and the father of Zerubbabel, as indicated in Luke 3:27. These relationships place him within a direct familial line significant to the Messiah's ancestry, though no further family details are given.
scriptureSignificance: Rhesa's significance lies in his position within the Messiah's genealogy, affirming the fulfillment of God's promise through a documented ancestral line. His mention in Luke 3:27 connects him to key figures who played roles in God's redemptive plan, emphasizing the historical and theological continuity culminating in Jesus Christ. Thus, Rhesa serves as a link in the divine lineage that validates Christ's messianic identity.
